subject: Real-time UX & concurrency: recap + next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Li <sam.li@veridium.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya@veridium.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Real-time UX & concurrency: recap + next steps

Thanks for the time today — quick recap from our call and proposed next steps. High-level: Veridium's primary constraint is real-time conversational UX for customer-facing agents (voice -> ASR -> LLM -> TTS) where tail latency spikes are causing customer-visible delays.

Pain points we heard:
- p95 generation latency currently ~1.4s for short prompts but spikes to 2.8–3.5s under load (peak hours)
- concurrency limits: live agent UI supports 50 simultaneous sessions; expected growth to 150 in Q2 with seasonal bursts to 300
- streaming UX: partial responses lose coherence when we chunk requests; customers expect token-level streaming to UI with <200ms inter-token gaps
- existing stack: in-house microservices on GKE, model hosted on preemptible GPUs with manual batching; no KV cache or prefix cache today

Success criteria you outlined:
- p95 end-to-end (model+network+middleware) <= 800ms for 95% of baseline sessions
- support sustained 150 concurrent real-time sessions with bursts to 300 without >20% degradation in p95
- token-level streaming that feels continuous to agents (inter-token latency <200ms)

Immediate next steps we proposed:
1) Engineering deep-dive: 60m session w/ your infra + our runtime engineers to share perf-profile artifacts and QPS patterns (Ben + Rishi + your infra lead). Goal: validate where most of the p95 is incurred (network, batching, KV cache miss, model kernel).
2) Share perf capture: you to send a 48h sampling of requests (timestamps, avg seq length, qps over time). We suggested a CSV with sample rows — attachment stub below is an example format.
3) Pilot proposal: a 4-week dedicated trial on Redwood Dedicated with pinned capacity and streaming enabled, plus a short load test to reproduce spikes.

Attachments: sample perf CSV format (perf_snapshot_qps.csv), brief planning heatmap (ma-planning-heatmap.pdf).

Can we schedule the engineering deep-dive Thursday or Friday this week? Ben will propose times.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sam Li <sam.li@veridium.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@veridium.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Real-time UX & concurrency: recap + next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is a helpful summary. Quick clarifications and additions:

- The 1.4s p95 is what our model infra reports for single request runs; our users feel it closer to 2–2.5s because of middleware queuing and network hops (we have a separate inference gateway).
- Concurrency: 50 current live agent sessions, 150 planned in Q2, bursts to ~320 during marketing pushes.
- Prompts: median prompt length is ~40 tokens, tail to 300 tokens for some diagnostic flows.
- We do use a simple Redis-layer cache but not used for KV cache (only request-level caching for identical queries).

I'll upload the sampling CSV by EOD tomorrow — it will include per-request receive/timestamp, seq length, and the gateway queue time.

Thursday works for the engineering deep-dive; available 10–11am or 2–3pm PT.

- Sam
Sam Li
Director of Product, Veridium AI
sam.li@veridium.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sam Li <sam.li@veridium.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@veridium.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Real-time UX & concurrency: recap + next steps

Thanks — quick engineering note ahead of Thursday:

Preliminary hypothesis on p95 contributors (based on what Marissa / Sam shared):
- 40–55%: gateway queuing and head-of-line when concurrency approaches the soft limit (your gateway serializes some requests into single worker pools)
- 25–35%: model decode latency under small-batch scenarios; some model kernels favor larger batch sizes (tradeoff with inter-token latency)
- 10–20%: network RTTs between regions (we should validate region routing)

Two practical artifacts that would accelerate troubleshooting if Sam can share before the call:
1) 48h CSV sample (timestamps, seq_length, gateway_queue_ms, model_decode_ms, region) — as Marissa requested.
2) A curl-based streaming example (small prompt -> stream tokens) so we can reproduce the inter-token gaps locally.

Also, for the pilot sizing I propose: pinned 8xA10G (or equivalent) with continuous batching and a KV prefix cache enabled for repeated conversational context. We'll bring a reproducible load script that ramps to 300 concurrent short sessions with the same prompt distribution you described.

I'll attach a tiny perf snapshot we run internally to illustrate batch size vs p95 tradeoff (attachment: perf_snapshot_qps.csv).

See you Thursday — Ben will send the invite.

Rishi
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
